title: Prenatal Environmental Stress, Placental Oxidative Stress, and Fetal Brain Development: A Proposed Econeurobiological Framework
content: Environmental and psychosocial conditions during pregnancy may influence neurodevelopment through interacting maternal and placental processes. This critical narrative review examines placental oxidative stress and mitochondrial regulation within a prenatal econeurobiological framework. Author-curated literature was supplemented by targeted bibliographic and original-source checks spanning environmental exposures, placental mechanisms, prenatal imaging, and childhood development. The synthesis distinguishes physiological redox signaling from oxidative injury and connects antioxidant defenses, trophoblast metabolism, and mitochondrial quality control with placental exchange and signaling. Experimental research supports selected links between maternal stress, placental oxidative responses, and offspring outcomes. Human biomarker and imaging studies provide complementary associations, including inconsistent and null findings, but do not establish placental oxidative mediation in humans. The framework distinguishes direct fetal exposure, altered placental function, and pathways involving obstetric complications, while retaining postnatal conditions as contributors to later performance. Its contribution is to specify which exposure–response relationships are supported and which require prospective testing. Temporally aligned biological sampling, developmental imaging, and functional follow-up are needed to determine when placental redox processes contribute to neurodevelopmental vulnerability. Antioxidant effects in experimental models motivate mechanistic investigation but do not establish clinical prevention of neurodevelopmental disorders.
